items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel, with a playful Halloween edge. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: Narrator
You'll see thousands of pumpkins tonight.
Narrator
But the first jack-o'-lanterns were never pumpkins... So what were they?
Narrator
Turnips. And it all started on one small hill in Ireland.
Narrator
So how did an Irish turnip end up on every American porch?
Narrator
Rewind. County Meath, Ireland. The Hill of Ward, once called Tlakh-ta.
Narrator
People may have gathered here since about one thousand B C.
Narrator
Old Irish texts link it to Sow-in: the end of harvest, the start of winter, on the night of the thirty-first of October.
Narrator
The story goes, a great fire was lit here... and torches carried it to hills across the land.
Narrator
That night, spirits were said to walk. So people carved scary faces... into turnips.
Chars
[grumpy, sulky little turnip, whiny and fed up] Why is it always me?
Narrator
Then, in the eighteen hundreds, Irish emigrants crossed the Atlantic to America.
Narrator
They brought the tradition. But America had something better than turnips.
Narrator
Pumpkins. Bigger, softer, and way easier to carve.
Chars
[proud, cheerful, chunky pumpkin, deep and delighted] Finally... a job I'm good at.
Narrator
This year, Americans are expected to spend about thirteen point five billion dollars on Halloween.
Narrator
So the world's spookiest night... began as a bonfire on one quiet Irish hill.
Chars
[grumpy, sulky little turnip, smug and slow] I was here first... Remember that.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
